heroHeadline: 27 Days to Kickoff — France Squad Named (Mbappe Confirmed); Japan Announces (Mitoma Out, Tomiyasu Returns); Iran Holds Grand Farewell in Tehran
heroSubtitle: Didier Deschamps announced France's final 26-man squad on May 14 in Paris — his last selection as Les Bleus head coach. Kylian Mbappe is confirmed as captain despite hamstring management by Real Madrid; Eduardo Camavinga (Real Madrid) and Randal Kolo Muani (PSG) are excluded. Ousmane Dembele leads a star-studded attack alongside new faces Rayan Cherki, Desire Doue, and Michael Olise. Japan coach Hajime Moriyasu named his 26-man squad on May 15, with Brighton's Kaoru Mitoma the most prominent absentee — ruled out by a hamstring injury; Takehiro Tomiyasu returns after nearly two years away and Yuto Nagatomo is selected for a fifth World Cup. Belgium also announced on May 15, with Romeo Lavia among the notable absentees (Red Devils in Group G vs Iran, New Zealand, Egypt). Iran held a grand public farewell ceremony on May 14 at Tehran's Enghelab Square — thousands attended, the 2026 kit was unveiled, and federation president Mehdi Taj described it as 'the best send-off in four World Cup campaigns.' The team departs for a training camp in Antalya, Turkey (warm-up vs Gambia May 29) before traveling directly to the US; no visas have been issued to any Iranian player or staff — the FIFA-Taj Zurich meeting on May 20 is the last formal channel before the June 1 squad deadline. Coming up: Brazil squad (May 18, Ancelotti); Germany (May 21); England (May 22, Tuchel, Wembley — Ben White ruled out, MCL); USMNT (May 26, NYC, FOX Sports); FIFA publishes all 48 squads June 2.
